Stages of Meiosis 1

Prophase 1
Chromosomes condense and thicken.
Homologous chromosomes pair up side-by-side in a process called synapsis to form a tetrad or bivalent.
Crossing over occurs where non-sister chromatids exchange genetic pieces, creating new genetic combinations.
The nuclear envelope breaks down and spindle fibers form. 


Metaphase 1
Paired homologous chromosome pairs (tetrads) line up along the middle (equator) of the cell.
Chromosomes orient randomly, which creates independent assortment and adds to genetic variety. 


Anaphase 1
Spindle fibers pull homologous chromosome pairs apart toward opposite poles of the cell.
Sister chromatids remain joined together at their centromeres. 


Telophase 1 and Cytokinesis
Chromosomes arrive at the opposite poles of the cell.
The nuclear membrane may reform around the chromosomes.
Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm, resulting in two separate haploid daughter cells
